name: Brow lift (surgical)
lead: A surgical brow lift, also called a forehead lift, browlift or browplasty, is a cosmetic operation that raises a low or drooping eyebrow and softens horizontal forehead lines. It is also used when a heavy brow obstructs the upper visual field.[1] Techniques include endoscopic, coronal, hairline (pretrichial), temporal, direct, mid-forehead and transblepharoplasty approaches.[1]

In looksmaxxing communities it is classed as 'hardmaxxing' (surgical and procedural enhancement). Forum members discuss it mainly as part of the upper-third and eye-area toolkit, often alongside blepharoplasty, and often as one item in multi-procedure trips abroad.[2][3] Proponents describe a higher brow position and a more open eye area as attractive; the published literature on brow lifts concerns aging, ptosis and patient satisfaction rather than attractiveness ideals in general.[4][5]

Published research includes case series of endoscopic and direct brow lifts and studies of non-surgical alternatives such as botulinum toxin and energy-based devices. Complications are described in the literature as uncommon but include numbness, hair loss at incision sites, asymmetry and scarring, depending on technique.[1][6]

paras: The procedure repositions the eyebrow and surrounding forehead soft tissue upward. Wikipedia describes it as treating a drooping brow that can impair vision and as softening deep forehead lines.[1] The brow tissue is released and then fixed in a higher position using sutures, screws, tissue adhesives or absorbable implants, depending on the surgeon and technique.[1][6]

Endoscopic brow lifts use several short incisions behind the hairline and a camera-guided instrument; Wikipedia describes about three to five incisions. The coronal technique uses a long incision across the scalp and was popular in the 1980s and 1990s but is described as less favored today.[1] Other approaches include the hairline (pretrichial) lift, the temporal lift aimed at the outer brow, the internal lift performed through an upper-eyelid incision, and the direct brow lift, in which skin is removed just above the brow.[1]

A published personal series of 538 patients compared fixation techniques for endoscopic brow lifts,[6] and a study in the British Journal of Ophthalmology examined the direct brow lift's efficacy, complications and patient satisfaction.[7]

A 2009 study in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery examined how eyebrow position and shape change with age,[8] and a 1996 study related brow lift outcomes to aesthetic ideals for eyebrow height and shape in women.[9] Both are often cited in discussions of what brow position is considered attractive, though they concern a specific surgical population and ideal.

Botulinum toxin injections can raise the outer brow by weakening muscles that pull it down; a 2000 case series of 22 patients tested this directly.[10] Wikipedia notes that many people choose injections repeated every four to six months instead of surgery, and that injections are sometimes used after surgery to extend results.[1] Ultrasound devices have also been studied for brow lifting as part of full-face and neck skin tightening.[11]

According to Wikipedia, complications are described as rare and usually minor when performed by a trained surgeon. Numbness was most common after direct brow lifts, hair loss after endoscopic lifts, and hairline elevation or reduced scalp sensation after coronal lifts. In about 1% of endoscopic cases surgeons convert to the open method. Infection and bleeding are risks of any surgery.[1]
Brow lift surgery has also been reported to alter migraine symptoms in some patients when the corrugator muscle is resected, an observation that prompted anatomical research on headache triggers.[12]

On looksmax.org, brow lifts appear in forum posts about combined surgical trips. One member described flying to Antalya, Turkey for a package that included a brow lift among other facial procedures, with a stated cost of about US$15,000, and was asked how to find surgeons and to post before-and-after photos.[2] Other threads ask for feedback about lateral brow lifts and discuss botulinum toxin as a brow-raising measure.[13][14] Members also post about early recovery, with one asking whether a swollen, 'uncanny' look at 16 days after multiple procedures is normal.[15]

Human studies include a rater-blinded prospective cohort of ultrasound skin tightening that assessed brow lift as an outcome,[11] a prospective case series of botulinum toxin for temporal brow lift,[10] and surgical series of endoscopic and direct brow lifts.[6][7]

Registered trials include a Phase 4 trial of Dysport for brow lifting (NCT01401803, 24 participants),[16] a terminated trial of the Zift device for lifting facial tissue (NCT03055819),[17] trials of Sofwave and Matrix Pro energy devices for eyebrow lift (NCT04969380, NCT06640998),[18][19] a trial of scar treatment after direct brow lift (NCT02032641),[20] and a planned trial of thread-assisted brow suspension (NCT07879456).[21] Results are not summarized here where not published in the sources consulted.

lore.intro: Brow lifts are discussed on looksmax.org mainly as one element of eye-area and upper-third surgery, often inside multi-procedure packages abroad.[2][13]

claims.claim: A higher or more lateral brow position improves facial attractiveness
claims.believers: Members seeking feedback on lateral brow lifts and combined eye surgery say a lifted brow opens the eye area and improves the look of the upper third.[13][2]
claims.experts: Surgical literature relates brow height and shape to aging and to ideals in women, and reports patient satisfaction with specific techniques; it does not establish a general attractiveness effect.[8][9][7]

claims.claim: Botulinum toxin can serve as a non-surgical brow lift
claims.believers: Forum threads discuss injecting around the brow to raise its tail as a lower-commitment alternative.[14]
claims.experts: A 2000 case series of 22 patients tested brow elevation after toxin injection,[10] and registered Phase 4 trials have examined toxin for brow lifting.[16]

claims.claim: Bundling many procedures abroad is a practical route to a large change
claims.believers: One poster described a single trip combining a brow lift with jaw, lip, cheek and dental work, citing a cost of about US$15,000.[2]
claims.experts: Published sources cited here do not evaluate multi-procedure medical travel. Surgical series report complications for individual brow lift techniques.[1][6]

card.summary: Surgery that raises a drooping brow and opens the eye area; well-documented in the plastic surgery literature, popular in forum surgery packages.
card.aka: Forehead lift, browplasty, endoscopic brow lift
card.note: Surgical risks include numbness, hair loss at incisions, scarring and asymmetry.

quick.overview:
A surgical brow lift repositions the eyebrow and forehead tissue higher. It is used for drooping brows that crowd the eye and for forehead lines, and looksmaxxing forums treat it as part of eye-area hardmaxxing.

Techniques range from endoscopic and coronal lifts to direct and temporal lifts. Non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin and ultrasound devices are also studied.
quick.mechanism: The surgeon releases the brow tissue and fixes it in a higher position using incisions at the hairline, temple, brow or upper eyelid, depending on the technique.
quick.risks: Reported complications include numbness, hair loss, hairline elevation, scarring, asymmetry, infection and bleeding. Rates vary by technique and surgeon, and the literature describes serious complications as uncommon.
